response.sql: WITH per_state AS (SELECT c.State AS State, SUM(i.Total) AS state_total, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId WHERE i.InvoiceDate >= '2010-06-22 00:00:00' AND i.InvoiceDate <= '2012-06-26 00:00:00' GROUP BY c.State) SELECT SUM(state_total) AS total_sum, AVG(invoice_count * 1.0) AS avg_invoices_per_state FROM per_state

assumptions.assumption: Customers with no state (NULL State) form one group, and that group counts as one state in the average. GROUP BY puts all NULLs together. Empty-string states, if any, are treated as their own distinct value.
The date range is compared as text and includes both ends. An invoice dated '2012-06-26 10:00:00' is after the upper bound string, so it is excluded.
The average is taken over the per-state groups that have at least one matching invoice. States with no invoices in the range are not counted.
